rationale: One more deterministic step, aimed at the entry that actually opened the joint configuration in the finding's history. Applying a JointImplicit change whose only change removes node 4 - a node that is not a member of the voters - leaves the node in a joint configuration: the draft-side case reports joint=true, auto_leave=true, voters still [1,2,3] and outgoing_size == incoming_size == 3. So a configuration change with no effect on the voter set still enters joint consensus, which means it also requires a leave-joint entry to exit, and by the knowledge recorded last turn that leave is proposed only by a node that is leader when it applies the change. That is the concrete way the history in the finding came to hold a joint-enter change with no leave anywhere: the first change was a no-op joint entry whose proposer did not live long enough as leader to leave the configuration, and the next leader's guard then admitted a second joint-enter change. I request isolated execution of this case so the no-op-enters-joint behavior is receipt-backed; it is the last link in the mechanism that the existing receipts do not already carry.

scope.description: Adds a deterministic case (TestAssuranceNoopJointRemoval) to the fixed harness: one voter built with newTestRaft(1,10,1,newTestMemoryStorage(withPeers(1,2,3))) is handed a ConfChangeV2 with Transition=JointImplicit whose single change removes node 4, which is not a member of the configuration; one CA_EVENT reports whether the tracker is joint, the AutoLeave flag, the voter list and the sizes of the outgoing and incoming voter sets. Probes A-C, the sweep, the joint-change-order case, the stale-guard case and the noop case compose the same harness.
assumptions: Everything comes from the snapshot's own facilities (newTestRaft, newTestMemoryStorage, withPeers, applyConfChange); no production logic is modified.
The change is applied directly rather than proposed, so the case establishes the resulting configuration state for that change, not how a cluster reaches it.
Node 4 is absent from the voter set by construction, so the change alters no membership; the question is only whether the transition still enters joint consensus.

experiment.prefix: r := newTestRaft(1,10,1,newTestMemoryStorage(withPeers(1,2,3))); r.applyConfChange(&pb.ConfChangeV2{Transition: JointImplicit, Changes: [{Type: RemoveNode, NodeId: 4}]}); then emit CA_EVENT noop_joint_removal with joint (len(Config.Voters[1]) > 0), auto_leave, voters, outgoing_size and incoming_size.
experiment.revision_reason: Same investigation with another deterministic case added (TestAssuranceNoopJointRemoval) to observe whether a joint-entering change that alters no membership still creates a joint configuration; a draft-side run reported joint=true, auto_leave=true, voters=[1,2,3], outgoing_size=3 and incoming_size=3, which is construction feedback only and is why isolated execution is requested.
